title: Height Using Distance
description: Calculates the height of an object using the horizontal distance and the angle of elevation.

example.question: Find the height of a tower if the distance is 20 m and the angle of elevation is 45°.

note: Use the tangent ratio when height and distance are involved.

title: Distance Using Height
description: Calculates the horizontal distance from the height of an object and the angle of elevation.

example.question: Find the distance from a tower of height 30 m if the angle of elevation is 30°.

note: Divide the height by tan θ to find the horizontal distance.

title: Line of Sight Using Height
description: Calculates the line of sight or slant distance using height and the angle of elevation.

example.question: Find the line of sight if the height is 12 m and the angle is 30°.

note: The hypotenuse represents the observer's line of sight.

title: Angle of Elevation
description: The angle formed between the horizontal line and the observer's line of sight when looking upward.

example.question: A person looks at the top of a tower. The angle formed with the horizontal is 40°. Identify the angle.
example.solution: The angle is called the angle of elevation.

title: Angle of Depression
description: The angle formed between the horizontal line and the observer's line of sight when looking downward.

example.question: A person standing on a building looks down at a car. The angle with the horizontal is 35°. Identify the angle.
example.solution: The angle is called the angle of depression.
